title: throughput-latency-scratchpad-aisha
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for latency/throughput experiments. Not formal — rough logs + immediate takeaways.

Goal: Find sensible defaults for batch_size, concurrency, and quantization profile for small-to-medium conversational workloads (avg seq 256, bursts to 1024). Prefer p95 < 150ms for single-turn 128 tokens and cost <= baseline by 15%.

Env:
- Service: dedicated pool noisybox-1 (A100-40GB, single-GPU nodes)
- Local bench tool: rwinfer-bench v0.9.1 (docker image rw/bench:0.9.1)
- Model variants tested: redwood-v1-small, redwood-v1-medium-fp16, redwood-v1-medium-int8, llama-2-13b-q4f32 (for compare)
- Network: colocated in us-west1, 0.8ms cross-host avg
- KV cache: tested cold vs warm (warm = previous 100 requests priming)

Command examples (used):
- rwinfer-bench --model redwood-v1-medium-fp16 --seq 256 --batch 1 --concurrency 8 --tokens 1024 --stream=false --warm-kv=false
- rwinfer-bench --model redwood-v1-medium-int8 --seq 512 --batch 4 --concurrency 16 --tokens 2048 --stream=true --warm-kv=true

Raw run excerpts (median/p95 in ms, throughput tokens/sec):
1) redwood-v1-small, seq=128, batch=1, conc=8, cold-kv:
   median=32ms, p95=78ms, tokens/s=7500
2) redwood-v1-medium-fp16, seq=256, batch=1, conc=8, cold-kv:
   median=86ms, p95=180ms, tokens/s=2100
3) redwood-v1-medium-int8, seq=256, batch=1, conc=8, cold-kv:
   median=74ms, p95=150ms, tokens/s=2400
4) redwood-v1-medium-int8, seq=256, batch=4, conc=16, warm-kv:
   median=68ms, p95=112ms, tokens/s=8600
5) llama-2-13b-q4f32, seq=256, batch=1, conc=8, warm-kv:
   median=210ms, p95=420ms, tokens/s=900
6) redwood-v1-medium-int8, seq=1024, batch=8, conc=32, warm-kv, streaming:true:
   median=520ms, p95=980ms, tokens/s=11k (note: streaming hides some tail latency upswing)

Observations (raw):
- INT8 path on medium model consistently reduces median and p95 vs FP16 ~10-20% on our workload.
- Batching (batch=4-8) + higher concurrency gives big throughput win but must be balanced with p95 SLOs; batch=4 + conc=16 was a sweet spot for seq<=256.
- KV cache warm dramatically reduces p95 for multi-turn/chat workloads (p95 drops ~30-50% in many runs).
- Llama-2 13B still far heavier cost/latency; useful as a quality reference only.
- Streaming reduces perceived latency at user-side but server-side p95 still high for long seqs; need separate SLO definitions (per-first-byte vs final-token).

Mini CSV snapshot (model,seq,batch,conc,warm_kv,median_ms,p95_ms,tokens_per_s):
redwood-v1-small,128,1,8,false,32,78,7500
redwood-v1-medium-fp16,256,1,8,false,86,180,2100
redwood-v1-medium-int8,256,1,8,false,74,150,2400
redwood-v1-medium-int8,256,4,16,true,68,112,8600
redwood-v1-medium-int8,1024,8,32,true,520,980,11000
llama-2-13b-q4f32,256,1,8,true,210,420,900

Quick conclusions / recommendations for product defaults (scratch):
- Hosted default profile for convo medium: model=redwood-v1-medium-int8, batch=4, concurrency=16, kv_cache=enabled, streaming=enabled (gives p95 ~110ms for short turns, excellent token/sec).
- For strict p95 <100ms targets, prefer batch<=2 and concurrency<=8, or downgrade to redwood-v1-small for short-turn UIs.
- Provide separate SLO metrics: time-to-first-byte (TTFB) and end-to-end final-token latency. Educate customers about streaming masking final-token tails.

Anomalies / flaky runs:
- 2025-02-16 10:17 run: sudden p95 spike to 400ms on medium-int8 batch=4 conc=16. Logs show GC events on node and a kernel fallback to slower matmul (linked_artifacts PR above). Root-cause suspected: kernel selection mismatch when seq distribution had many 1024 sequences interleaved.
- Observed ~2% of requests show 10x latency due to network retries when we saturated per-node ingress; add more fine-grained queue depth metrics.

Open questions / next experiments:
- Re-run medium-int8 with per-request seq-prioritization (small seqs first) to see tail improvement.
- Evaluate H100 nodes (noisybox-2) for long-seq workloads: expect better p95 for 1024+ but need cost model.
- Microbench kernel-level traces for the spike — correlate with kernel selection table (see rw/bench PR 142).
- Test quantization-awareness in routing: route long sequences to fp16 variants automatically to reduce tail.

Notes-to-self:
- Push quick note to #perf with csv snapshot and link to PR 142.
- Add simple dashboard: per-route p95, tokens/s, cold vs warm split.
- Keep this scratchpad lean; will formalize into perf-run-2025Q1.md if we get stable signal.

End of scratchpad.

-- Aisha
